claims.text: Conventional solid-state sintering of single-phase ZrB2 requires temperatures above 2300 °C.
Single-phase ZrB2 has strong Zr–B and B–B bonding.
A boron-rich, low-melting transient liquid-phase sintering aid can consolidate ZrB2 below 1700 °C.
The product obtained with the transient liquid-phase aid will remain single-phase ZrB2.
The transient liquid phase forms at ZrB2 grain boundaries during sintering.
The grain-boundary liquid phase promotes densification and heals interfacial defects.
Transient-liquid formation facilitates particle rearrangement at lower sintering temperatures.
Transient-liquid formation enhances interparticle bonding at lower sintering temperatures.
Transient-liquid-phase sintering reduces residual porosity and microstructural defects.
Reduced porosity and improved grain boundaries increase resistance to high-temperature oxidation.
Reduced porosity and improved grain boundaries increase resistance to liquid plating-metal corrosion.
Below-1700 °C transient-liquid-phase-sintered ZrB2 will have higher density than both conventionally sintered ZrB2 and ZrB2 sintered below 1700 °C without the aid.
Below-1700 °C transient-liquid-phase-sintered ZrB2 will have fewer grain-boundary or microstructural defects than both comparison materials.
Below-1700 °C transient-liquid-phase-sintered ZrB2 will outperform both comparison materials in high-temperature oxidation tests.
Below-1700 °C transient-liquid-phase-sintered ZrB2 will outperform both comparison materials during prolonged exposure to liquid plating metal.
The proposed process is applicable below 1700 °C under an inert or reducing atmosphere.
